summary: Kosai Fukushima (1928–2011) was a Buddhist studies scholar who taught Paul L. Swanson. He held posts at Otani University, including Dean of Students (attested 1985) and professor (attested 1992).

Kosaku Hamada (1881–1938) specialized in archaeology, history, Sinology, and Japanology. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1902–1905), he held posts at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University (~1913–1938), teaching Taichiro Kobayashi and Seiichi Mizuno.

Kosei Ishii (born 1950) specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Waseda University under Akira Hirakawa (~1974–1985), later earning a doctorate there (1994). He served at Waseda, Komazawa Junior College (1994–2006), and Komazawa University (~1999; professor emeritus 2006–2021).

Kosei Tada (1938–2017) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held positions at Taisho University (~1973–2009) and served as board chairman of the Society for the Study of Buddhist Culture (attested 2004).

Kosen Imakita (1816–1892) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied under Togai Fujisawa, Kyokuso Hirose, Shoen Daisetsu, and Gisan Zenrai, served as abbot at Eikō-ji (1858) and Engaku-ji (1875–1892), and taught Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki and Soyen Shaku.
Koshin Suzuki (born 1959) is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies at Taisho University and served as a researcher there (attested 1995–1998).

Koshiro Tamaki (1915–1999) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at the Fifth Higher School and the University of Tokyo (DLitt 1959), he held professorships at the University of Tokyo (1964–1976), Tohoku University (~1973–1976), and Nihon University (1979–1986).

Kosho Mizutani (1928–2014) was a Buddhist studies scholar educated at Ryukoku and Bukkyo universities. He served at Bukkyo University as associate professor (~1956–1974) and president (~1979–1995), and led Bukkyo Kyoiku Gakuen (~1995–2011) and Tokai Gakuen (~1998–2011).
Kosho Murakami (born 1933) is a scholar in the fields of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Kodo Sawaki and Hideki Yukawa.

Koshu Itabashi (1927–2020) was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied at Sendai Daiichi High School, the Imperial Japanese Naval Academy, and Tohoku University (~1949–1953) under Teruji Ishizu (~1948–1953).

Kosuke Nakazawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who taught Guohui Shi. He held posts at Rissho University as professor (attested 2001) and professor emeritus (attested 2026), and was a member of the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra.

Kotatsu Fujita (1928–2023) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at the University of Tokyo and Harvard. He held professorships at Hokkaido University (~1967–1992) and served as president of Sapporo Otani Junior College (1992).

Kotetsu Yoshida (born 1941) is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He has served as professor emeritus at Taisho University (attested 2014) and as an advisor at Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (attested 2014).
Koun Kajiyoshi (1904–1984) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1926–1929) and held a post at Taisho University (~1949–1974).
Koyo Sakaino (1871–1933) worked in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He founded the Bukkyo Seito Doshikai and held posts at Toyo University (~1918–1933) and Komazawa University.
Koyo Shimizu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shoko Takeuchi. He served as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 1995).

Koyu Tamura (1931–2022) was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees including a doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Nishogakusha University (1965) and Toyo University (1972; professor emeritus 1977–2000), and taught Shigeki Moro.

Kozen Shaku (1849–1924) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied under Senmyō. He served as head priest at Gyokuri-ji (1870–1881) and Sange-ji (1882), founded Shakuson Shofukai, and taught Ekai Kawaguchi and Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki.

Kozui Otani (1876–1948) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and Central Asian studies. Educated at Kyoritsu Gakusha and Gakushuin under Eun Maeda, he served as the 22nd Abbot of Nishi Hongan-ji (1903–1914) and taught Bunkyo Aoki.

Krishna Kamal Bhattacharya (1840–1932) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Sanskrit College and University and Presidency College, Kolkata (~1857–1860), later holding posts at Presidency College (1862–1872) and Surendranath College (1891–1903).
